title: Independent cotangent classes cut out a component of codimension two
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $M$ an invertible module, $s_2,s_3\in\Gamma(X,M)$, and $t\in X$ a point whose stalk $\mathcal O_{X,t}$ is regular local. Suppose $U\subset X$ is an affine neighbourhood of $t$, $e$ a free generator of $M$ on $U$, and $f_0,f_1\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ the coefficients of the restrictions of $s_2,s_3$ relative to $e$. Assume the germs of $f_0,f_1$ lie in $\mathfrak m_t$ and their classes in $\mathfrak m_t/\mathfrak m_t^2$ are linearly independent over $\kappa(t)$. Then there is an irreducible closed subset $W\subset X$ containing $t$, maximal among irreducible closed subsets of $|Z(s_2)|\cap|Z(s_3)|$, with $\operatorname{coheight}(W)=2$. Scheme conventions are [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], invertibility is [def-sc-invertible-module], regularity is [def-weil-regular-scheme], and zero schemes are [def-pc-zero-scheme]. No field, connectedness, global regularity, noetherianity away from $t$, or finite morphism is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 3, independent differentials and the codimension-two component

proof.text: Extend the independent cotangent classes to a basis. Nakayama gives generators of the maximal ideal from the lifted basis. In the quotient by the selected independent lifts, the remaining basis vectors generate its maximal ideal, bounding its embedding dimension from above. The quotient dimension bound gives the reverse bound, so that quotient is regular. This argument is proved as a private helper and does not assume a regular-system-of-parameters theorem.

The pair quotient and the first-parameter quotient are regular local domains. Thus the pair ideal P and the principal ideal Q generated by the first parameter are prime. Independence implies the first parameter is nonzero and the second is not in Q. Q has height one, Q is strictly below P, and the two-generator height theorem bounds P from above by two. Thus P has height two.

Contract P from the stalk to the affine coordinate ring. Localization preserves its height and identifies all smaller primes. A prime below the contraction containing the pair ideal extends to a prime containing P, hence equals P after extension; contraction gives equality. The contraction is therefore minimal over the pair ideal. The coefficient formulas for the ideal sheaves identify its generic point with a point of both zero supports.

Take W to be the closure of the contracted prime point in X. The maximal ideal at t contains that prime, so t belongs to W. W lies in both closed zero supports. Any larger irreducible closed subset Z of their intersection has generic point specializing to t, hence lies in U at its generic point. The corresponding prime is below the contracted prime and contains the pair ideal; minimality makes the primes equal and hence Z=W. Coheight is preserved under the affine open immersion and equals the prime height, namely two.

theorem local_cotangent_pair_component
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible]
    (s₂ s₃ : Γ(M, ⊤)) (t : X) [IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk t)]
    (U : X.affineOpens) (htU : t ∈ U.1) (e : Γ(M, U.1))
    (he : Scheme.Modules.IsFreeGenerator e) (f : Fin 2 → Γ(X, U.1))
    (hs₂ : M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U.1 ≤ ⊤)).op s₂ = f 0 • e)
    (hs₃ : M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U.1 ≤ ⊤)).op s₃ = f 1 • e)
    (hf : ∀ i, X.presheaf.germ U.1 t htU (f i) ∈
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk t))
    (hind : LinearIndependent (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk t))
      (fun i ↦ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk t)).toCotangent
        ⟨X.presheaf.germ U.1 t htU (f i), hf i⟩)) :
    ∃ W : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds X,
      Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds X ↦
        (Z : Set X) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection M s₂).zeroLocus.support ∩
          (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection M s₃).zeroLocus.support) W ∧
      t ∈ (W : Set X) ∧ Order.coheight W = 2
